key_insight: LLM browser agents often completed sequencing prior authorization tasks but rarely withheld deficient cases for the correct reason, revealing a bias toward submission.
clinical_relevance: Automating exome/genome sequencing prior authorization could reduce administrative burden, but unreliable withholding may allow deficient requests to proceed.
method: Built a simulated payer portal and synthetic EHR with 836 compliant and deliberately deficient patient profiles.
Evaluated Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, and Claude Opus 4.5 on completion, form accuracy, and appropriate withholding.
Repeated evaluations twice on 100 profiles to assess run-to-run variability.
evidence_signal: Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5 achieved 95.5% and 93.7% task completion, respectively, yet first-run correct withholding across models was only 0–17.3%.
watch_item: Synthetic sandbox results may not generalize to clinical workflows, and substantial run-to-run variability makes dependable safety checks and human oversight important.
paper_title: Hard to Halt: Automation Bias in Agent-Driven Sequencing Prior Authorization Workflows
